plain: To set free from slavery or control

webster.text: To set free from servitude or slavery, by the voluntary act of the proprietor; to liberate; to restore from bondage to freedom; as, to emancipate a slave.

more.text: In ancient Rome, to set a son free from subjection to his father, and give him the capacity of managing his affairs, as if he was of age.

example.quote: This could not prevent Congress from interfering witb that property by laying a grievous and enormous tax on it, so as to compel owners to emancipate their slaves rather than pay the tax.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 17, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
